title: The Satanic Verses
author: Salman Rushdie
current_text: On 5 October 1988 India banned the novel's importation, after Syed Shahabuddin petitioned the government of Rajiv Gandhi. In November 1988 it was also banned in Bangladesh, Sudan and South Africa, and by December 1988 in Sri Lanka. In March 1989 it was banned in Kenya, Thailand, Tanzania, Indonesia and Singapore, and the last nation to ban it was Venezuela, in June 1989.

Banned by the Iranian government in 1988. On 14 February 1989 Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a fatwa calling for the death of Rushdie and his publishers. The fatwa was declared permanent in 2006; the bounty on Rushdie's head was raised to $3.4 million in March 2016.
Import ban issued 5 October 1988 by the Rajiv Gandhi government following a petition from MP Syed Shahabuddin. Possession of the book was not criminalised.

Banned in Malaysia by the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) under the Printing Presses and Publications Act. Gazetted 1989-03-30 (P.U. (A) 94). Publisher: The Penguin Group. Printer: Richard Clay Ltd,. Language: INGGERIS. Possession of the book carries up to three years' imprisonment or a fine of approximately $7,400.
Banned in Kenya in March 1989 (Wikipedia, citing Netton).
Turkey prohibited importing the book and any Turkish translation; it remains unpublished in Turkish. Aziz Nesin's serialized excerpts triggered the 1993 Sivas massacre.
Barred in Jordan as blasphemous against Islam following Khomeini's fatwa; named in 2010 as the most-requested banned book in the country.
Banned March 1989. Possession of the book carries up to one month's imprisonment or a fine.
